classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every stable coherent system with R=2rank(F)>0 require the displayed slope bound. mu' stability and exact constants c,b are absent; decimal 1.3818 is not an exact replacement. Cannot formulate the literal endpoint.
statement_utf8:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ be a smooth quintic surface and let $h=c_1(\mathcal{O}_S(1))$. A coherent system on $S$ is a morphism $(\mathcal{O}_S^{\oplus R}\to F)$; let $\mu'$ denote the slope stability function used in the source.

**Clifford-type bound conjecture.** For every $\mu'$-stable coherent system $(\mathcal{O}_S^{\oplus R}\to F)$ with

$$
R=2\operatorname{rank}(F)>0,
$$

one has

$$
\frac{c_1(F)\cdot h}{R}>\frac{5}{8}+\frac{c}{b}=1.3818\cdots.
$$

This conjecture is intended to provide the inequality needed for the double-tilting construction of a Gepner-type stability condition on the corresponding matrix-factorization category. The source does not prove the bound.
technical_assessment: For every stable coherent system with R=2rank(F)>0 require the displayed slope bound. mu' stability and exact constants c,b are absent; decimal 1.3818 is not an exact replacement. Cannot formulate the literal endpoint.
title: Clifford-type bound for stable coherent systems on quintic surfaces

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For both ADE constructions require the identically zero genus-two G-function. The decomposition does not define Q_p,c_p or G independently. Checking a few ADE types would not prove both unbounded families; no short uniform cancellation identified.
statement_utf8:
Let $M$ be a Frobenius manifold associated to an ADE singularity or to an extended affine Weyl group of ADE type. Its genus two free energy has a decomposition

$$
\mathcal{F}_2=\sum_{p=1}^{16}c_pQ_p+G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx}),
$$

where the $Q_p$ are contributions represented by genus zero correlation functions and $G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx})$ is the genus two $G$-function.

**Genus two G-function vanishing conjecture.** For every such $M$,

$$
G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx})=0.
$$

The conjecture concerns the vanishing of the non-explicit genus two contribution in the free energy for Frobenius manifolds arising from ADE singularities and extended affine Weyl groups of ADE type. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
technical_assessment: For both ADE constructions require the identically zero genus-two G-function. The decomposition does not define Q_p,c_p or G independently. Checking a few ADE types would not prove both unbounded families; no short uniform cancellation identified.
title: Genus two G-function vanishing conjecture for ADE Frobenius manifolds

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: The placement of 'for all n' relative to iff is unclear and pattern lengths/classes are unrestricted. Binary-tree spine refinement is not defined. For small n both counts vanish, so a pointwise-iff reading is suspect; do not credit this wording objection.
statement_utf8:
Let $\tau$ and $\mu$ be permutation patterns, and let $A_n(\tau)$ and $A_n(\mu)$ denote their total numbers of occurrences among permutations in $S_n(132)$. Associate to each pattern its binary tree $T(\tau)$ or $T(\mu)$, and let its spine structure be ordered by refinement order. **Rudolph's popularity conjecture.** For all $n$, 
$$
A_n(\tau) \le A_n(\mu)
$$
 if and only if the spine structure of $T(\tau)$ is less than or equal to the spine structure of $T(\mu)$ in refinement order. This conjecture seeks a complete characterization of the popularity order on 132-avoiding permutation patterns; Rudolph had previously proved equality of popularities when the corresponding trees have the same spine structure.
technical_assessment: The placement of 'for all n' relative to iff is unclear and pattern lengths/classes are unrestricted. Binary-tree spine refinement is not defined. For small n both counts vanish, so a pointwise-iff reading is suspect; do not credit this wording objection.
title: Rudolph's popularity conjecture for 132-avoiding patterns

statement_utf8:
Let $q=e^{2\pi i z}$, and let

$$
\Delta_k(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\tau_k(n)q^n\in S_k^{\operatorname{new}}(\Gamma_0(1))
$$

be a newform, where $k\in\{12,16,18,20,22,26\}$. **Lehmer's conjecture.** For every such $k$ and every positive integer $n$,

$$
\tau_k(n)\neq0.
$$

For $k=12$, this is Lehmer's question about the nonvanishing of the Ramanujan tau function, and the source states that it remains open, as do analogous questions for the other listed newforms.

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Limit over all square sizes requires a specified firefighter budget, move order and optimal saving policy. rho is described informally without those rules. Finite grid optimization cannot establish the exact limit; retain HOLD.
statement_utf8:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and let $P_n\square P_n$ be the Cartesian product of two such paths. Write $\rho(G)$ for the expected percentage of vertices saved when a fire starts at a uniformly random vertex of the finite graph $G$. **The square-grid surviving-rate conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho(P_n\square P_n)=\frac{5}{8}.
$$

The paper proves matching lower bounds of $5/8+o(1)$ and an upper bound differing by less than $0.0136$, so the conjecture remains open.
technical_assessment: Limit over all square sizes requires a specified firefighter budget, move order and optimal saving policy. rho is described informally without those rules. Finite grid optimization cannot establish the exact limit; retain HOLD.
title: The surviving-rate conjecture for square grids

b_9(32k+13)\equiv 0\pmod{12}.

statement_utf8:
Let an **overpartition** of a nonnegative integer be a partition in which the first occurrence of each part may be overlined, and let $\bar{p}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$, with $\bar{p}(0)=1$. For every integer $n\geq 0$, **Hirschhorn–Sellers' conjecture.**

$$
\bar{p}(40n+35)\equiv 0 \pmod {40}.
$$

This is a Ramanujan-type divisibility conjecture for the overpartition function. The conjecture is stated in the source as an open conjecture; the paper proves it using generating functions and modular-form methods.

statement_utf8:
Let $X$ be a Niemeier root system with Coxeter number $m$. A representation is a **doublet** if it is the direct sum of two copies of one representation, and a **sextet** if it is the direct sum of six copies of one representation. **Doublet and sextet conjecture.** The representation $K^X_{r,-D/4m}$ is a doublet if and only if $D\ne0$ and $D\ne-n\lambda^2$ for every integer $\lambda$ and every $n$ listed in the source's discriminant table for $X$. If $X=A_8^3$, then $K^X_{r,-D/4m}$ is a sextet if and only if

$$
D\ne-27\lambda^2
$$

for some integer $\lambda$. The source presents this as a conjecture based on observed multiplicity patterns; no resolution is supplied.

The preceding results show non-existence for $4\leq n\leq 10$ and force $\omega_U=1$ whenever the category exists in the cases studied. **Existence and non-existence conjecture.** The technique used for the preceding uniqueness and non-existence theorems should show that ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$ exists only if $\omega_U=1$ for all $1\leq n<\infty$, and that ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$ does not exist for all $4\leq n<\infty$. Let $K_{4,36}$ denote the order-five variational-equation entry obtained by transporting the jet along the cycle $\gamma=\gamma_-^{-1}\gamma_+^{-1}\gamma_-\gamma_+$. Let $(\Lambda,\lambda)$ be the parameters of the Friedmann–Robertson–Walker Hamiltonian, and let $n=0,1$ refer to the exceptional cases listed in the source's equation (exc). **Nonvanishing conjecture.**

K_{4,36}\neq 0

for every value of $(\Lambda,\lambda)$ except for $n=0,1$ in (exc). Hence, the order-five variational equations yield the first obstruction to integrability in $H$. statement_utf8:
Let $k\geq 4$. Consider the linear relations among the generators of the weight-$k$, length-two component $\operatorname{gr}^{\operatorname{W},\operatorname{L}}_{k,2}\operatorname{q\mathcal{M}\mathcal{Z}}$. **The relation-count conjecture.** For every weight $k\geq 4$, the number of such linear relations equals

$$

The authors verified the claim for $k\leq 20$, where this method produced all observed length-two relations; the assertion is proposed on the basis of that computation.

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each positive n and every n-term consecutive interval strictly between n^2 and(n+1)^2 require a prime. This is a strong uniform short-interval assertion; bounded primality computations cannot resolve arbitrary n. No tractable deterministic mechanism.
statement_utf8:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider $n$ consecutive integers $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n$ satisfying

$$
n^2<a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n<(n+1)^2.
$$

**Consecutive-integers prime conjecture.** At least one of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ is prime.

This conjecture concerns the existence of primes in intervals between consecutive squares and would imply Legendre's, Brocard's, Andrica's, and Oppermann's conjectures, as well as related prime-gap bounds. The paper reports verification for every $n$ with $1\leq n\leq 1,193,806,023$, but the general assertion remains open.
technical_assessment: For each positive n and every n-term consecutive interval strictly between n^2 and(n+1)^2 require a prime. This is a strong uniform short-interval assertion; bounded primality computations cannot resolve arbitrary n. No tractable deterministic mechanism.
title: The consecutive-integers prime conjecture between consecutive squares

statement_utf8:
Let a **cycle-maximal triangle-free graph** be a triangle-free graph to which no edge can be added without creating a triangle. For a graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ denote the balanced complete bipartite graph. **The bipartite Turán graph conjecture.** The cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs are exactly the bipartite Turán graphs

$$
K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}
$$

for all $n$. The conjecture was verified by exhaustive computer search for $n\leq 13$; it proposes that balanced complete bipartite graphs maximize the number of cycles among cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs.

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: The two inequalities quantify a,b,n1,n2 but lack admissible parameter range and winning-coalition definition. Relative Banzhaf denominators can degenerate on boundary cases. Cannot screen strictness uniformly until the game model is restored.
statement_utf8:
Let $n_1,n_2$ be the numbers of players of the two types, and let $Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)$ denote the relative Banzhaf power index of a player of type $2$ in the corresponding complete simple game. **Relative Banzhaf monotonicity conjecture.**

For $b\geq 1$,

$$
Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)-Bz_2(a,b-1,n_1,n_2)>0.
$$

For $a\geq 2$,

$$
Bz_2(a-1,b,n_1,n_2)-Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)\geq 0,
$$

with equality for $b=0$ and a strict inequality otherwise. The conjecture would imply a corollary analogous to the stated ordering result for the relative Banzhaf index; it is supported in the source by verification for all $n\leq 100$.
technical_assessment: The two inequalities quantify a,b,n1,n2 but lack admissible parameter range and winning-coalition definition. Relative Banzhaf denominators can degenerate on boundary cases. Cannot screen strictness uniformly until the game model is restored.
title: Monotonicity conjecture for the relative Banzhaf power index

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For odd-part partitions of a common size require equivalence of class order with reversed dominance. The twisted class order and twist are absent; ordinary symmetric-group classes alone do not define it. No source-independent monotonicity argument.
statement_utf8:
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions with only odd parts, and let $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$ and $\mathcal{O}_\mu$ be the corresponding cuspidal classes of the symmetric group. The dominance order on partitions is defined by $\mu \trianglelefteq \lambda$ when, for every positive integer $k$, the sum of the first $k$ parts of $\mu$ is at most the sum of the first $k$ parts of $\lambda$. **Dominance-order conjecture.** The classes satisfy

$$
\mathcal{O}_\lambda \leq \mathcal{O}_\mu
$$

if and only if

$$
\mu \trianglelefteq \lambda.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the partial ordering on cuspidal twisted conjugacy classes agrees, under the parametrization by odd-part partitions, with the dominance order. It had been checked by computer for $n\leq 10$ in the source.
technical_assessment: For odd-part partitions of a common size require equivalence of class order with reversed dominance. The twisted class order and twist are absent; ordinary symmetric-group classes alone do not define it. No source-independent monotonicity argument.
title: Dominance-order conjecture for cuspidal classes of the symmetric group

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every order bound and every indicated partition interval pair require the stretching length comparison. LGL derivative roots define the usual grids. Interlacing alone does not compare these stretched adjacent lengths uniformly; no exact all-order certificate found.
statement_utf8: Let $[a,b]$ be an interval, let $L=L_{[a,b]}:[a,(a+b)/2]\to[a,b]$ be given by $L(x)=2x-a$, and let $\{{\cal G}^{\mathrm{LGL}}_N\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be the family of Legendre–Gauss–Lobatto grids. A family of symmetric grids has property $\mathbf{Str}_{\bar N}$ if, for every $N\leq\bar N$, every interval $I\in\mathcal{P}({\cal G}_N)$ with $I\subset(a,a+(b-a)/4]$, and every $I'\in\mathcal{P}({\cal G}_N)$ such that $L(I)\cap I'\neq\varnothing$, one has $|I'|\leq|L(I)|$. **The LGL stretching property conjecture.** The family $\{{\cal G}^{\mathrm{LGL}}_N\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ has property $\mathbf{Str}_{\bar N}$ for every $\bar N\in\mathbb{N}$. This is supported by numerical verification through order $\bar N=2000$; the assertion for all orders remains open.
technical_assessment: For every order bound and every indicated partition interval pair require the stretching length comparison. LGL derivative roots define the usual grids. Interlacing alone does not compare these stretched adjacent lengths uniformly; no exact all-order certificate found.
title: The LGL stretching property conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Demand both quotient monotonicities at all orders, but first clause only says fixed k/relevant indices and omits its valid endpoints. Root interlacing is weaker than ratio monotonicity. No finite sweep would discharge the all-order claims.
statement_utf8: Let $\xi^N_0<\xi^N_1<\cdots<\xi^N_N$ be the LGL points, let $\Delta^N_k=[\xi^N_k,\xi^N_{k+1}]$, and define $q_k^N=|\Delta^N_k|/|\Delta^N_{k-1}|$ for the relevant indices. The family has property $\mathbf{MQ}_{\bar N}$ if $q_k^N\leq q_k^{N+1}$ for $N<\bar N$ and fixed $k$, and $q_k^N\geq q_{k+1}^N$ for $1\leq k\leq\lfloor(N-3)/2\rfloor$ and $N\leq\bar N$. **The LGL quotient monotonicity conjecture.** The LGL grids have property $\mathbf{MQ}_{\bar N}$ for every $\bar N\in\mathbb{N}$. Numerical evidence verifies the property through $\bar N=2000$; its validity for all orders remains open.
technical_assessment: Demand both quotient monotonicities at all orders, but first clause only says fixed k/relevant indices and omits its valid endpoints. Root interlacing is weaker than ratio monotonicity. No finite sweep would discharge the all-order claims.
title: The monotonicity conjecture for LGL interval quotients

For positive integers $r,k,n$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_r(12^{t_1}3^{t_2}\dots s^{t_{s-1}}(s+1)^{t_s}1,k,n)$ denote the corresponding extremal function. **Extremal-function conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ depending on $t$ such that, for every $r\geq C$, 
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_r(12^{t_1}3^{t_2}\dots s^{t_{s-1}}(s+1)^{t_s}1,k,n)=rn.

 The conjecture extends the exact-value result established immediately beforehand for the pattern treated in the theorem, predicting the same linear extremal value for this broader family of forbidden sequences. The supplied text gives no resolution beyond presenting it as a conjecture.

statement_utf8: Let $P_n$ be a path, $C_n$ a cycle, and let $P_n^6$ be the graph obtained by connecting a vertex of $C_6$ to a terminal vertex of $P_{n-6}$. Among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, the cycle $C_n$ has maximal energy if $n\leq 7$ and $n=9,10,11,13$ and $15$. **Caporossi's conjecture.** For all other values of $n$, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is $P_n^6$. The conjecture was stated as a conjecture on maximal energy among unicyclic graphs and is completely solved in the source's subsequent theorem, which adds the exceptional case $n=4$, where $P_4^3$ is maximal.

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all primes p>=3 and p all respectively, and implicit m>=1, demand the two congruences. m is not explicitly bound. Primary Theorems1.2/1.3 cover p>=5 and all p for s18; remaining p=3 for s7 lacks an all-m bridge. No credit for proved subfamilies.

source_coverage.scope: Theorems1.2/1.3 and initial proof of1.3 through binomial congruence reduction; remainder and dependencies unread

statement_utf8:
Let

$$
s_7(n)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n}{k}^2\binom{n+k}{k}\binom{2k}{n}
$$

and

$$
s_{18}(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}(-1)^k\binom{n}{k}\binom{2k}{k}\binom{2(n-k)}{n-k}\left[\binom{2n-3k-1}{n}+\binom{2n-3k}{n}\right],
$$

with $s_{18}(0)=1$. **Cooper's conjecture.** For every prime $p\geqslant3$,

$$
s_7(mp)\equiv s_7(m)\pmod{p^3},
$$

and, for every prime $p$,

$$
s_{18}(mp)\equiv s_{18}(m)\pmod{p^2}.
$$

These congruences are sporadic-sequence analogues of known congruences for Apéry numbers. The paper proves the $s_7$ congruence for $p\geqslant5$ and the $s_{18}$ congruence for all primes; the $s_7$ case for $p=3$ remains open.
technical_assessment: For all primes p>=3 and p all respectively, and implicit m>=1, demand the two congruences. m is not explicitly bound. Primary Theorems1.2/1.3 cover p>=5 and all p for s18; remaining p=3 for s7 lacks an all-m bridge. No credit for proved subfamilies.
title: Cooper's one-term supercongruences for the sporadic sequences s_7 and s_{18}

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every complete Riemannian plane, unique disjoint geodesic through each exterior point should force flatness. The condition is global; local curvature or a special metric family is insufficient. No bounded full-plane rigidity mechanism identified.
statement_utf8: Let $(\mathbb{R}^2,g)$ be a complete Riemannian plane. For a geodesic $\gamma$, say that a geodesic through a point $x\notin\gamma$ is disjoint from $\gamma$ if it does not intersect $\gamma$. **Knieper's conjecture.** If for every geodesic $\gamma$ and every point $x$ outside $\gamma$ there exists a unique geodesic through $x$ that does not intersect $\gamma$, then $g$ is flat. This is a rigidity conjecture in differential geometry, attributed to G. Knieper and stated in 1991. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
technical_assessment: For every complete Riemannian plane, unique disjoint geodesic through each exterior point should force flatness. The condition is global; local curvature or a special metric family is insufficient. No bounded full-plane rigidity mechanism identified.
title: Knieper's rigidity conjecture for complete Riemannian planes

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each theta>=0 with matched kappa require distributional convergence as n grows. Infinite triangulation law T_kappa and local topology are not defined. Euler degree matching is necessary but does not establish tightness or identification.
statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{T}_{n,g}$ be the set of rooted triangulations of genus $g$ with $n$ vertices, and let $T_{n,g}$ be uniformly distributed in $\mathcal{T}_{n,g}$. For $\kappa\in(0,\frac{2}{27}]$, define

$$
f(\kappa)=E\left[\left(\operatorname{degree\ of\ the\ origin\ in\ }\mathbf{T}_{\kappa}\right)^{-1}\right].
$$

For $\theta\geq0$, let $\kappa\in(0,\frac{2}{27}]$ satisfy $f(\kappa)=(6(1+2\theta))^{-1}$. **Parameter identification conjecture.**

$$
T_{n,[\theta n]}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}\mathbf{T}_{\kappa}.
$$

This sharpens the introductory conjecture by matching the finite and infinite models through the inverse degree of the root; the required strict monotonicity and the resulting convergence are not proved in the paper.
technical_assessment: For each theta>=0 with matched kappa require distributional convergence as n grows. Infinite triangulation law T_kappa and local topology are not defined. Euler degree matching is necessary but does not establish tightness or identification.
title: Parameter identification conjecture for high-genus triangulation limits

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every complete interpolating sequence require a positive constant uniform in omega and N. The dual functions phi_k are not defined and constant dependence needs source confirmation. A Dirichlet-kernel special case does not control arbitrary Riesz sampling systems.
statement_utf8:
Let $\{t_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be an ordered complete interpolating sequence for $\mathcal{PW}_{\pi}^{2}$. **Logarithmic lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $C_{12}$ such that

$$
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\left|\sum_{k=-N}^{N}e^{\mathrm{i}\omega t_k}\widehat{\phi_k}(\omega_1)\right|\,d\omega_1\geq C_{12}\log(N)
$$

for all $\omega\in[-\pi,\pi]$ and all $N\in\mathbb{N}$.
The conjecture is presented as a possible explanation for pointwise-sampling divergence, while the supplied text gives no resolution evidence; it therefore remains open in the database.
technical_assessment: For every complete interpolating sequence require a positive constant uniform in omega and N. The dual functions phi_k are not defined and constant dependence needs source confirmation. A Dirichlet-kernel special case does not control arbitrary Riesz sampling systems.
title: Logarithmic lower-bound conjecture for complete interpolating sequences

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All g,h coefficients obey one formal product, but the BPS count construction/divisibility conventions are not specified. Formal coefficient expansion computes the prediction rather than identifies the enumerative invariants. Large geometric dependency chain; park.
statement_utf8:
Let $r_{g,h}$ denote the BPS count associated to a class $\beta$ on a K3 surface whose norm square satisfies

$$
\langle\beta,\beta\rangle=2h-2.
$$

Let $q$ and $y$ be formal variables. **Katz–Klemm–Vafa product formula.** The BPS counts $r_{g,h}$ are uniquely determined by

$$
\sum_{g\geq 0} \sum_{h\geq 0} (-1)^g r_{g,h}(y^{\frac{1}{2}} - y^{-\frac{1}{2}})^{2g}q^h = \prod_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(1-q^n)^{20} (1-yq^n)^2 (1-y^{-1}q^n)^2}.
$$

This formula is the generating-series form of the Katz–Klemm–Vafa prediction and packages the BPS counts for all genera and arithmetic genera. It follows from the preceding conjectural independence from divisibility and is the central product formula for K3 BPS invariants.
technical_assessment: All g,h coefficients obey one formal product, but the BPS count construction/divisibility conventions are not specified. Formal coefficient expansion computes the prediction rather than identifies the enumerative invariants. Large geometric dependency chain; park.
title: The Katz–Klemm–Vafa product formula for BPS counts of K3 surfaces

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every dimension and normed real space require Liouville volume>=4^n/n!. Unit balls make the symmetric volume product precise. Low-dimensional polytopes or cube equality are instances; no sharp arbitrary-dimensional inequality route.
statement_utf8:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be an $n$-dimensional normed space, let $(X^*,\|\cdot\|^*)$ be its dual, and let $B$ and $B^{\circ}$ be the unit balls of $X$ and $X^*$, respectively. Write $\nu(X)$ for the Liouville volume of $B\times B^{\circ}\subset X\times X^*$, also called the Mahler volume or volume product. **Mahler's volume product conjecture.** For every $n$-dimensional normed space $X$,

$$
\nu(X)\geq\frac{4^n}{n!}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the sharp lower bound for the volume product of centrally symmetric convex bodies, with equality attained by the hypercube and, non-uniquely in the broad formulation, its relevant affine counterparts. It was conjectured by Mahler in 1939 and remains an open problem in convex geometry.
technical_assessment: For every dimension and normed real space require Liouville volume>=4^n/n!. Unit balls make the symmetric volume product precise. Low-dimensional polytopes or cube equality are instances; no sharp arbitrary-dimensional inequality route.
title: Mahler's volume product conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every n>1 and each of seven explicit triples require integer sum divisible by n binom(2n,n). Exact hypergeometric sums make finite checking possible but seven all-n divisibilities need uniform certificates. No creative-telescoping certificate established.
statement_utf8:
Let the **Franel numbers** be $f_n=\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^n {n\choose j}^3$. **Guo's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n>1$ and every

$$
(a,b,c)\in\{(9,4,5),(5,2,16),(9,2,50),(5,1,96),(6,1,320),(90,13,896),(102,11,10400)\},
$$

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(ak+b)c^{n-k-1}{2k\choose k}f_k\equiv0\pmod{n{2n\choose n}}.
$$

The authors report verification for $n$ up to $500$, but no proof or resolution is supplied.
technical_assessment: For every n>1 and each of seven explicit triples require integer sum divisible by n binom(2n,n). Exact hypergeometric sums make finite checking possible but seven all-n divisibilities need uniform certificates. No creative-telescoping certificate established.
title: Guo's positive-base Franel-number congruence family

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every I>=8 require I disjoint(I+2)-element Golomb rulers packing the entire interval of size I(I+2). Counting supplies lower bound only; all-I packing needs a uniform construction. Finite library through150 supplies no such construction.
statement_utf8:
Let $H(I,J)$ be the least positive integer $n$ such that there exist $I$ disjoint Golomb rulers, each a $J$-subset of $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$. **Regularity conjecture.** For every integer $I\geq8$,

$$
H(I,I+2)=I(I+2).
$$

Thus the conjecture predicts regular disjoint Golomb rulers in this parameter range. The paper reports that the assertion has been confirmed computationally for $I\in\\{8,\ldots,150\\}$, but treats the unrestricted statement as conjectural.
technical_assessment: For every I>=8 require I disjoint(I+2)-element Golomb rulers packing the entire interval of size I(I+2). Counting supplies lower bound only; all-I packing needs a uniform construction. Finite library through150 supplies no such construction.
title: The regularity conjecture for $H(I,I+2)$

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Universal positive infimum across all nonzero-length metrized graphs uses the undefined tau functional. The additional strict1/108 claim is stronger than positivity and must not replace it. No uniform energy lower-bound proof identified.
statement_utf8:
Let $\Gamma$ be a metrized graph, let $\ell(\Gamma)=\int_{\Gamma} dx$ be its total length, and consider metrized graphs with $\ell(\Gamma)\neq 0$. **Baker and Rumely's tau lower bound conjecture.**

$$
\text{inf}_{\Gamma}\frac{\tau(\Gamma)}{\ell(\Gamma)}>0,
$$

where the infimum is taken over all metrized graphs $\Gamma$ with nonzero total length. The conjecture asserts the existence of a universal positive lower bound for the tau constant normalized by total length. The paper states a refinement asserting the explicit bound $\tau(\Gamma)>\frac{1}{108}\ell(\Gamma)$ for every metrized graph; the abstract describes $\frac{1}{108}$ as the conjectural lower bound, while the general conjecture is not presented as resolved.
technical_assessment: Universal positive infimum across all nonzero-length metrized graphs uses the undefined tau functional. The additional strict1/108 claim is stronger than positivity and must not replace it. No uniform energy lower-bound proof identified.
title: Baker and Rumely's tau lower bound conjecture for metrized graphs

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each epsilon>0 demand uniform nonsquare-D cancellation in the given growth range plus the D=0 asymptotic. The two claims need different analyses; elementary absolute bounds lose cancellation. No complete analytic continuation/spectral mechanism supplied.
statement_utf8:
For integers $D$ and $l>0$, define

$$
S(D;3l)=\sum_{\substack{x\pmod{3l}\\4x^2\equiv D\pmod{3l}}}e\left(\frac{4x^3-3Dx}{27l^2}\right),
$$

and, for $Y\geq1$, define

$$
F(D;Y)=\sum_{l\leq Y}\frac{S(D;3l)}{\sqrt l}.
$$

**Exponential-sum conjecture.** If $D$ is not a square, then, uniformly for $D\ll Y^{1+\varepsilon}$,

$$
F(D;Y)\ll Y^{\varepsilon}.
$$

Moreover,

$$
F(0;Y)=3Y^{1/2}+O\left(Y^{5/18+\varepsilon}\right).
$$

These estimates describe the cancellation expected in the nonsquare case and the more precise main term for $D=0$; they are motivated by theoretical and computational evidence and are used to analyze the sum $T_S”(N,X)$.
technical_assessment: For each epsilon>0 demand uniform nonsquare-D cancellation in the given growth range plus the D=0 asymptotic. The two claims need different analyses; elementary absolute bounds lose cancellation. No complete analytic continuation/spectral mechanism supplied.
title: Conjecture on exponential sums associated with Mordell curves

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All finite characteristically simple groups are included, including abelian C_p^k and small groups. Beauville property is undefined and standard small abelian exceptions make the iff suspect as written. Domain correction is uncredited; no nonabelian all-family proof route.
statement_utf8: A **characteristically simple group** is a finite group isomorphic to $H^k$, where $H$ is finite simple and $k$ is a positive integer. **The characteristically simple Beauville group conjecture.** For every finite characteristically simple group $G$, $G$ is Beauville if and only if $G$ is 2-generated and is not isomorphic to the alternating group $A_5$. The source reports verification for several families and computationally for all such groups of order at most $10^{30}$, while leaving the general statement unresolved.
technical_assessment: All finite characteristically simple groups are included, including abelian C_p^k and small groups. Beauville property is undefined and standard small abelian exceptions make the iff suspect as written. Domain correction is uncredited; no nonabelian all-family proof route.
title: The characteristically simple Beauville group conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each r>=0 classify all positive integer pairs with gap2^r and cube-full product. Obvious powers of2 give the asserted family, but do not exclude odd prime factors. Cube-full consecutive number constraints obstruct a short all-size classification.
statement_utf8:
For positive integers $A$ and $B$, call $AB$ **cube-full** when every prime divisor of $AB$ occurs to exponent at least $3$. **The cube-full Catalan-type equation conjecture.** Let $r\geq0$ be an integer. The Diophantine equation

$$
\begin{cases}
A-B=2^r,\\
AB\text{ is cube-full},
\end{cases}
$$

has no solutions for $r=0$, and has the unique solution $(A,B)=(2^{r+1},2^r)$ for $r\geq1$. The source reports computational verification up to $B<A<10^6$, while the assertion for all $r$ remains open.
technical_assessment: For each r>=0 classify all positive integer pairs with gap2^r and cube-full product. Obvious powers of2 give the asserted family, but do not exclude odd prime factors. Cube-full consecutive number constraints obstruct a short all-size classification.
title: The cube-full Catalan-type equation conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Infinitely many primes must have no cube-full gap representation, and29 must be least. Even checking one fixed prime requires excluding unbounded A,B. Bounded searches do not certify nonexistence or infinitude; no full route.
statement_utf8:
For positive integers $A$ and $B$, call $AB$ **cube-full** when every prime divisor of $AB$ occurs to exponent at least $3$. **The prime-gap cube-full equation conjecture.** There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the Diophantine equation

$$
\begin{cases}
A-B=p,\\
AB\text{ is cube-full},
\end{cases}
$$

has no solutions; moreover, the least such prime is $29$. The source states this as a conjecture supported by computation, and no proof of either assertion is given.
technical_assessment: Infinitely many primes must have no cube-full gap representation, and29 must be least. Even checking one fixed prime requires excluding unbounded A,B. Bounded searches do not certify nonexistence or infinitude; no full route.
title: The prime-gap cube-full equation conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Exists universal C for every k and every strongly Ck-connected tournament ensuring all ordered disjoint k-pair linkages. Exhaustive small tournaments cannot settle linear connectivity. Path routing requires a substantial uniform combinatorial theorem; no small certificate route.
statement_utf8: A **tournament** is a directed graph with exactly one directed edge between any two distinct vertices. A tournament is **strongly $r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves a strongly connected directed graph. It is **$k$-linked** if, for every two disjoint sets of vertices $\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}$ and $\{y_1,\dots,y_k\}$, there are vertex-disjoint directed paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ such that $P_i$ goes from $x_i$ to $y_i$. **Kühn, Lapinskas, Osthus, and Patel's conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that every strongly $Ck$-connected tournament is $k$-linked. The conjecture proposes that the known $10^4k\log k$ connectivity bound can be reduced to a linear bound in $k$, beyond the reach of the sorting-network method described in the surrounding discussion.
technical_assessment: Exists universal C for every k and every strongly Ck-connected tournament ensuring all ordered disjoint k-pair linkages. Exhaustive small tournaments cannot settle linear connectivity. Path routing requires a substantial uniform combinatorial theorem; no small certificate route.
title: Kühn, Lapinskas, Osthus, and Patel's linear connectivity conjecture for tournaments

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every separated set in R3 and every unit-distance pair with both kissing degrees12 require at least4 common neighbors. Although local, it is a continuous configuration problem with24 incident positions. No exact feasible fewer-than4 construction or exhaustive geometric obstruction identified.
statement_utf8:
Let $Z\subset{\mathbb{R}}^3$ satisfy $|z'-z|\geq 1$ for all $\\{z,z'\\}\subset Z$. For each $z\in Z$, define its nearest-neighbor set by

$$
N(z):=\left\\{z'\in Z:|z'-z|=1\right\\}.
$$

**Common-neighbor conjecture.** If $z,z'\in Z$ satisfy $\\#N(z)=\\#N(z')=12$ and $z\in N(z')$, then

$$
\\#(N(z)\cap N(z'))\geq 4.
$$

This remains an open problem and could provide a route to eliminate the necessity of the three-body potential $V_3$ in the analysis of face-centered cubic crystallization.
technical_assessment: For every separated set in R3 and every unit-distance pair with both kissing degrees12 require at least4 common neighbors. Although local, it is a continuous configuration problem with24 incident positions. No exact feasible fewer-than4 construction or exhaustive geometric obstruction identified.
title: The twelve-neighbor common-neighbor conjecture for close-packed configurations

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all knots and each of15 named Rig quandles require endpoint color equality. Finite operation tables are not present; all-knot extension would require a faithful embedding or extension theorem verified for those tables. Finite crossing data is not full scope.
statement_utf8:
A knot $K$ is **end monochromatic with a quandle $X$** when the colors induced at the two endpoints of a $1$-tangle representative of $K$ agree for every coloring by $X$. Let $X$ be one of the following Rig quandles:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&Q(12,1), && Q(20,3), && Q(24,3), && Q(24,4), && Q(24,5),\\
&Q(24,6), && Q(24,14), && Q(24,16), && Q(24,17), && Q(30,1),\\
&Q(30,16), && Q(32,5), && Q(32,6), && Q(32,7), && Q(32,8).
\end{aligned}
$$

**End-monochromaticity conjecture.** Every knot $K$ is end monochromatic with $X$.

The claim generalizes computations showing end monochromaticity for all knots through nine crossings for these quandles. It is used to control colorings of connected sums and to recover information from quandle cocycle invariants; the source gives no proof for all knots.
technical_assessment: For all knots and each of15 named Rig quandles require endpoint color equality. Finite operation tables are not present; all-knot extension would require a faithful embedding or extension theorem verified for those tables. Finite crossing data is not full scope.
title: End-monochromaticity conjecture for selected Rig quandles

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every knot require invariant support in even powers of Z4. The generating cocycle is selected by source example but absent. Reduction modulo2 might use a coboundary certificate, but no exact cocycle table available; no claimed certificate.
statement_utf8:
Let $X=Q(12,5)$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}_4$, and let $\phi:X\times X\rightarrow A$ be the generating $2$-cocycle chosen in the source's example. For a knot $K$, let $\Phi_\phi(K)$ denote its quandle cocycle invariant, viewed in the group ring $\mathbb{Z}[A]$ and written using a generator $u$ of $A$. **Q(12,5) cocycle-invariant conjecture.** For every knot $K$,

$$
\Phi_\phi(K)=a+bu^2,
$$

where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$. Computations through eight crossings show this restricted support and motivate the conjecture; the source does not establish it for all knots.
technical_assessment: For every knot require invariant support in even powers of Z4. The generating cocycle is selected by source example but absent. Reduction modulo2 might use a coboundary certificate, but no exact cocycle table available; no claimed certificate.
title: Cocycle-invariant support conjecture for the Rig quandle Q(12,5)

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every knot require no u or u5 terms of Z6 invariant. Specific cocycle and table absent. Unlike subgroup support, allowed exponents2,3,4 are not closed under addition; a naive closure/connected-sum argument needs actual realization data. HOLD.
statement_utf8:
Let $X=Q(12,10)$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}_6$, and let $\phi:X\times X\rightarrow A$ be the generating $2$-cocycle chosen in the source's example. For each knot $K$, write its quandle cocycle invariant in $\mathbb{Z}[A]$ as

$$
\Phi_\phi(K)=a+bu+cu^2+du^3+eu^4+fu^5,
$$

where $a,b,c,d,e,f\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $u$ represents a generator of $A$. **Q(12,10) cocycle-invariant conjecture.** For every knot $K$, the coefficients of $u$ and $u^5$ vanish:

$$
b=f=0.
$$

Computations through eight crossings show terms with exponents $2$, $3$ and $4$, but no terms with exponents $1$ or $5$. The conjecture asserts that these latter terms never occur.
technical_assessment: For every knot require no u or u5 terms of Z6 invariant. Specific cocycle and table absent. Unlike subgroup support, allowed exponents2,3,4 are not closed under addition; a naive closure/connected-sum argument needs actual realization data. HOLD.
title: Cocycle-invariant support conjecture for the Rig quandle Q(12,10)

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every n>=12 and admitted k demand exact graph equality iff odd n,k=n-1,n-4 composite. Prime graph adjacency is conventional but not specified. Source flags additive prime obstructions; checking cycle types gives a prime-sum condition rather than an all-n resolution.
statement_utf8:
Let $G=A_n$ and $H=(S_k\times S_{n-k})\cap G$, where $1<k<n$ and $p\leqslant k$ for every prime number $p\leqslant n$. **Prime-graph equality conjecture.** If $n\geqslant 12$, then

$$
\Gamma(G)=\Gamma(H)
$$

if and only if $n$ is odd, $k=n-1$, and $n-4$ is composite. This concerns the unresolved classification of when an alternating group and an associated intransitive maximal subgroup have the same prime graph; the paper notes that the problem is connected with difficult additive questions about representations of integers as sums of distinct primes.
technical_assessment: For every n>=12 and admitted k demand exact graph equality iff odd n,k=n-1,n-4 composite. Prime graph adjacency is conventional but not specified. Source flags additive prime obstructions; checking cycle types gives a prime-sum condition rather than an all-n resolution.
title: Prime-graph equality conjecture for intransitive subgroups of alternating groups

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all n>=2 and x in C_n require D(x)>=1, but neither configuration domain nor determinant normalization is defined. The n=2 example cannot select among inequivalent Atiyah-Sutcliffe analogues. Missing target, no replacement.
statement_utf8:
Let $C_n$ be the configuration space under consideration, and let $D(\boldsymbol{x})$ denote the associated determinant for $\boldsymbol{x}\in C_n$. **Determinant inequality conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$ and every $\boldsymbol{x}\in C_n$, one has

$$
D(\boldsymbol{x})\geq 1.
$$
 This is presented as a stronger conjecture, analogous to Conjecture 2 of Atiyah--Sutcliffe (2002), and it implies the linear independence conjecture. The inequality is verified in the paper for $n=2$, while the general case remains open.
technical_assessment: For all n>=2 and x in C_n require D(x)>=1, but neither configuration domain nor determinant normalization is defined. The n=2 example cannot select among inequivalent Atiyah-Sutcliffe analogues. Missing target, no replacement.
title: The determinant inequality conjecture for configurations of points

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All bases and X>=0 refer to unnamed HWM convergent notation and T_b, while exceptions in bases2,3,4 are omitted. Literal cannot determine its own valid parameter domain or digit endpoint. Finite continued fractions would not repair it.
statement_utf8:
Let $C_b$ be Champernowne's constant in base $b$, let $X\geq 0$, and let the $X$th HWM convergent be denoted by the notation used in the source. The integer sequence used to form $C_b$ contains the integers in base-$b$ order.

**HWM convergent calculation conjecture.** The HWM convergent calculates $C_b$ correctly until the integer $T_b(X+1)-2$ is reached, and calculates that integer as $T_b(X+1)-1$ instead.

This is the first conjecture in the paper's extension of the authors' earlier base-$10$ conjectures to arbitrary bases. The stated base-$2$, base-$3$, and base-$4$ exceptions are part of the surrounding discussion, but the parser supplied no resolution evidence.
technical_assessment: All bases and X>=0 refer to unnamed HWM convergent notation and T_b, while exceptions in bases2,3,4 are omitted. Literal cannot determine its own valid parameter domain or digit endpoint. Finite continued fractions would not repair it.
title: The HWM convergent calculation conjecture for Champernowne's constant

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every n compare three coefficients, but placeholders [...] and lambda4/ell0 multiplicity conventions are corrupt or absent. Expanding a guessed partition statistic would solve an invented statement. No computation/promotion.
statement_utf8:
Let $[...]$ range over partitions of $n$, let $h_{ij}$ be the hook length of $(i,j)$, and let $[...]$ denote the number of parts of $[...]$ equal to zero as defined in the paper. The 2-truncated hook-length expression is

$$
\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{\substack{h_{ij}\in\lambda\\h_{ij}=1,2}}\left(1-\frac{b}{h_{ij}^2}\right).
$$

**2-truncation correction conjecture.** For every $n$, its constant, $b$, and $b^2$ coefficients agree with those of

$$
\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\left[\lambda_4\frac{b^2-b^3}{16}+(1-b)^{\ell_0(\lambda)}\prod_{\lambda_j>1}\left(1-\frac{b}{2}\right)\right].
$$

This is reported as a numerical observation intended to identify a correction factor for the unmodified 2-truncation; the source gives no proof or resolution.
technical_assessment: For every n compare three coefficients, but placeholders [...] and lambda4/ell0 multiplicity conventions are corrupt or absent. Expanding a guessed partition statistic would solve an invented statement. No computation/promotion.
title: Correction-factor conjecture for the 2-truncated hook-length formula

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All tensor models and disclination lines are claimed, but corrupted7k/2 and71/2 notation, stability ordering and admissible models are undefined. Special disk result does not restore universal target. No technical endpoint available.
statement_utf8: Consider disclination lines in the Landau–de Gennes theory, including $7k/2$-disclination lines and the $71/2$-disclination line. **Half-integer disclination-line stability conjecture.** Among all the disclination lines, the $71/2$-disclination line is the most stable. The source notes that this is provable in a special two-dimensional disk setting and proposes that it is generally true for all tensor models of liquid crystals, so the general statement remains open.
technical_assessment: All tensor models and disclination lines are claimed, but corrupted7k/2 and71/2 notation, stability ordering and admissible models are undefined. Special disk result does not restore universal target. No technical endpoint available.
title: Stability conjecture for half-integer disclination lines

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all parallel alternations of length>=6 require Av(pi) deflatable. Deflatability and the exact parallel-alternation convention are absent. Individual witnesses do not yield a uniform witness for every length/orientation; no proved mechanism.
statement_utf8:
Let $pi$ be a **parallel alternation**, meaning a permutation whose entries alternate between two monotone subsequences, with $|pi|\geq 6$. For a permutation $pi$, let $\operatorname{Av}(pi)$ denote the class of permutations avoiding $pi$.

**Deflatability conjecture.** The class $\operatorname{Av}(pi)$ is deflatable.

This conjecture is motivated by explicit deflatability witnesses for several parallel alternations, including $246135$ and longer examples. The general assertion for all parallel alternations of length at least six remains open in the supplied source.
technical_assessment: For all parallel alternations of length>=6 require Av(pi) deflatable. Deflatability and the exact parallel-alternation convention are absent. Individual witnesses do not yield a uniform witness for every length/orientation; no proved mechanism.
title: Deflatability conjecture for parallel alternations

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For all integer n>=0 require each of five displayed Young graphs isomorphic to Y(11,7). Graph transition/retained-vertex definitions are absent. Affine carry-state templates could be a route only after definition and successor verification; not yet a justified hypothesis.
statement_utf8:
Let $Y(g,k)$ denote the Young graph associated with the base $g$ and multiplier $k$. **$Y(11,7)$ family conjecture.** For all $n\ge 0$, the Young graphs

$$
Y(2(n+2)(n+3)-1, 2(n+2)^2-1),\quad Y(23+20n, 13+12n),\quad Y(23+15n, 17+10n),
$$

$$
Y(26+12n, 10+4n),\quad\text{and}\quad Y(11+6n, 7+3n)
$$

are all isomorphic to $Y(11,7)$. These experimentally observed isomorphisms are part of the paper's computational study of equivalence classes of Young graphs; no proof or resolution is supplied.
technical_assessment: For all integer n>=0 require each of five displayed Young graphs isomorphic to Y(11,7). Graph transition/retained-vertex definitions are absent. Affine carry-state templates could be a route only after definition and successor verification; not yet a justified hypothesis.
title: Young graph isomorphism conjecture for the $Y(11,7)$ family

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every prime p demand first cyclotomic Z_p-layer class number1. Probabilistic heuristics or checking small conductors cannot bound all class groups. No discriminant-unit mechanism uniformly excludes nontrivial class number.
statement_utf8: For every prime $p$, let $\mathbb{B}_{p,1}$ be the first layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. **First-layer class-number conjecture.** For every prime $p$, the class number of $\mathbb{B}_{p,1}$ is $1$. The paper proves or conditionally verifies several initial cases and combines sieve estimates with Cohen–Lenstra heuristics to obtain a probability estimate of at least $75\%$. No proof for all primes is known.
technical_assessment: For every prime p demand first cyclotomic Z_p-layer class number1. Probabilistic heuristics or checking small conductors cannot bound all class groups. No discriminant-unit mechanism uniformly excludes nontrivial class number.
title: Class-number-one conjecture for the first layers of cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For every alpha>0 exists beta>0 and a sufficiently large threshold uniform over all sets of size>p^alpha. Square-root character-sum bounds address only larger sets; small positive alpha needs genuine pseudorandom cancellation. No complete route.
statement_utf8:
For primes $p\equiv1\bmod4$, let $\chi$ be the Legendre symbol modulo $p$. Define $\operatorname{PaleyDiscrepancy}[\alpha,\beta]$ to mean that, for every sufficiently large $p$,

$$
\left|\sum_{a,b\in S}\chi(a-b)\right|<|S|^{2-\beta}
$$

for every $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ with $|S|>p^\alpha$. **Chung's conjecture.** For each $\alpha>0$, there exists $\beta=\beta(\alpha)>0$ such that $\operatorname{PaleyDiscrepancy}[\alpha,\beta]$. This folklore conjecture appeared as Conjecture 2.2 in Chung (1994), with a proof for $\alpha>1/2$ given there, and has also been used in constructing a pseudorandom number generator. The source does not state a complete resolution for arbitrary $\alpha>0$.
technical_assessment: For every alpha>0 exists beta>0 and a sufficiently large threshold uniform over all sets of size>p^alpha. Square-root character-sum bounds address only larger sets; small positive alpha needs genuine pseudorandom cancellation. No complete route.
title: Chung's Paley discrepancy conjecture

classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each admissible nonempty peak set require all complex roots within radius m and real part>=-3. Peak polynomial/admissibility are not defined here. Finite numerical roots do not certify all sets; no universal coefficient/root-location mechanism derived.
statement_utf8:
Let $S$ be an admissible peak set, let $m=\max(S)$, and let $p_S(z)$ be its peak polynomial. A complex root is a number $z\in\mathbb C$ such that $p_S(z)=0$.

**Bounded-roots conjecture.** Every complex root of $p_S(z)$ lies in

$$
\{z\in\mathbb C: |z|\le m\text{ and }\operatorname{Re}(z)\ge -3\}.
$$

The conjecture is stronger than the positivity conjecture above and is presented as a proposed explanation for positivity of the binomial-basis coefficients. The paper reports experimental verification for all admissible peak sets with $\max(S)\le 15$, but does not prove the conjecture in general.
technical_assessment: For each admissible nonempty peak set require all complex roots within radius m and real part>=-3. Peak polynomial/admissibility are not defined here. Finite numerical roots do not certify all sets; no universal coefficient/root-location mechanism derived.
title: Bounded-roots conjecture for peak polynomials

statement_utf8:
Let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring, and let $J_n$ denote the ideal associated with the cyclic graph on $n$ vertices as in the paper. The **Stanley depth conjecture.** For all $n\geq 10$ satisfying $n\equiv 1\pmod{3}$,

$$
\operatorname{sdepth}(S/J_n)=\left\lceil\frac{n}{3}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture concerns the remaining congruence class in the authors' study of the Stanley depth of quotients by ideals associated with line and cyclic graphs; the stated examples support the formula, but the claim is not resolved in the supplied source.

title: Conjecture on the Stanley depth of cyclic graph edge ideals
